result.title: Trait Collapse in Text-to-Image Generation: Evaluating and Mitigating Personality Inconsistency in Visual Storytelling
result.comment: EMNLP 2026 Main Conference Paper. 26 pages, 5 figures
result.summary: In visual storytelling, a believable character must not only look consistent across scenes but also \textit{behave} in ways that reflect their personality. Current text-to-image (T2I) models preserve visual appearance effectively, yet consistently fail to maintain personality-relevant behavior---a failure we term \textit{trait collapse}. We show that conventional metrics (CLIP Score, DINO similarity) are blind to this failure, and that abstract personality descriptors and scene-level emotion labels do not produce consistent improvements over neutral prompts across models. To systematically diagnose trait collapse, we introduce \textbf{ViStoryBench-Personality}, a story-level benchmark combining an expert-validated Visual Cues Lexicon (Fleiss' $κ= 0.757$) with a six-dimensional metric suite covering personality alignment, cross-scene stability, and behavioral coherence. Evaluating seven T2I systems, we confirm a persistent semantic gap between abstract trait labels and visual evidence, and find that visual identity consistency does not imply personality consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose \textbf{Trait-Behavior-Visual (TBV)}, a training-free prompting framework that decomposes personality traits into renderable visual constraints. TBV improves Personality Alignment Score by up to $+22.1\%$, with larger gains in models with stronger language-conditioning capacity.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 ViStoryBench-Personality 基准与六维指标，诊断 T2I 模型在视觉故事中的人格行为不一致（「trait collapse」），并提出免训练的 TBV 提示框架把抽象人格特质分解为可渲染的视觉约束。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是 T2I 生成的角色人格一致性与提示分解，不涉及 VLM 推理状态、视觉证据的使用、动态计算或停止决策，也未提供可核查的表示或训练线索，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
